update public.meal set workflow_md=$m$*Serves 3 (2 carb-moderate adults + teen) · 1.18 kg compact tied MB3+ rib eye, 12 cm dia · Service 7:05pm, Sun 12 Jul · Register: classic, generous, restrained* ## Menu - Rib eye roast (reverse sear) - Duck-fat roast potatoes (split-roast) - Honey-glazed carrots (light honey) - Green beans, butter + lemon zest - Horseradish cream - Red wine jus (staged) ## Critical Path Potato pre-roast → beef low roast → beef rest (potato recrisp overlaps) → potato out → oven to max → beef blast → carve. Single Bosch oven; every oven transition is gated by the oven reaching temperature, not by elapsed time — the clock is the planning path, not a guarantee. Horseradish is made ahead and never gates service. **Failure prioritization:** Protect beef core temp and the final potato crisp. Governing rule — the beef's 40-min rest ceiling outranks potato recrisp duration and nominal service time. If a transition compresses the recrisp, pull potatoes at achieved crust; the beef blast does not wait. ## Oven Sequencing (single Bosch — state-gated) - 450°F / 230°C — potato pre-roast. Potatoes enter only once the oven actually reads 450°F. - 250°F / 121°C — beef low roast. After pre-roast, drop the setting and briefly vent the door (450→250 with door shut is slow); beef enters only once near 250°F. - ≥425–450°F / 220–230°C — potato recrisp. Begins once genuinely recovered. - Max / 500°F — beef blast. Begins once the oven reaches actual max. ## Parallel vs. Sequential - Parallel: carrots (induction 1), beans blanch-then-hold (induction 2), jus on outdoor gas burner (keeps both induction burners free). Horseradish done ahead. - Sequential (oven-bound): potato pre-roast → beef low → potato recrisp → beef blast. One owner at a time. ## T-Minus Timeline *Planning path, 7:05pm service. Beef pull temp is the master trigger; oven transitions are temperature-gated. The clock is the on-time estimate — the trigger band below governs deviation.*
TimeAction
Sat eveningCut + re-tie roast done, 1.18 kg. Dry-brine 12 g Diamond Crystal (1%), uncovered on rack, fridge, ~24 hr
3:45 pmBeef out of fridge (~70 min before roasting — takes surface chill off; do not wait for center to reach room temp). Make horseradish if not done
3:55 pmOven → 450°F. Parboil potatoes (baking soda), drain, rough, dry
~4:05 pmOnce oven reads 450°F: potatoes pre-roast, aim to finish ~4:40–4:45 — pale gold, set, not yet deeply crisp
~4:40–4:45 pmPotatoes out → hold uncovered, single layer, wire rack, room temp. Drop oven to 250°F, vent door briefly. (If beef start shifts later, delay the pre-roast rather than hold potatoes past 2 hr.)
4:45 pmJus stage 1: brown 1 sliced shallot (+ optional trimmings) in a little oil on outdoor gas; deglaze with wine, reduce by half; add stock, brief simmer, then off heat, covered
4:50 pmBeef: pat bone-dry, oil, pepper, insert probe (alarm 116°F)
~4:55 pmOnce oven near 250°F: beef in (~75–80 min, probe-governed)
6:05 pmJus stage 2: return to gas, finish stock reduction to a light nappe. Begin watching probe
6:15 pmBeef pulls at 119–120°F. Onto rack, rest uncovered. Oven → back up to 450°F. Fold low-roast drippings into jus
~6:28–6:30 pmOnce oven ≥425–450°F: potatoes back in, recrisp ~15–20 min — pull when deeply golden and audibly crisp, turning once. Watch the garlic/thyme
6:35 pmCarrots on induction 1; bean water to boil on induction 2
~6:40–6:43 pmJus stage 3: add drippings, strain, mount 20 g cold butter, hold warm on lowest gas. Blanch beans 4 min, shock, drain, hold
~6:48 pmPotatoes out at achieved crisp → hold on rack, room temp. Oven → max
~6:54 pmOnce oven at max: beef in, blast 5–8 min, crust-color-governed
6:57 pmToss beans butter + zest, low induction. Plate carrots
~7:00–7:02 pmBeef out when crust set. Thermapen-verify ~127–133°F. Add final-blast drippings to jus
7:05 pmHandling done — carve against grain. Plate; jus + horseradish to table
### Trigger band (governs deviation) - Pull 6:14–6:20: normal path, hold ~7:05 service. - Pull 6:10–6:13: advance potato exit, oven-to-max, and blast by the matching minutes; potatoes accept a shorter recrisp. - Pull before 6:10: advance the whole final sequence, accept earlier service. Don't extend the rest to protect 7:05. - Pull after 6:20: shift service later; carrots and beans wait, beef doesn't. *Verification: Beef rest 6:15→~6:54 = ~39 min, under 40 ✓. Potato recrisp sensory-governed ~15–20 min ✓. Jus staged with hold, not continuously reduced ✓. Blast + handling → 7:05 carve ✓. Transitions state-gated, none assumed instantaneous ✓.* ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDrift RiskCorrective
BeefRack, uncovered, room temp40 minOver-rest cools coreBlast reheats surface; Thermapen-verify post-blast
Potatoes (pre-roast)Wire rack, room temp, single layer~2 hrSurface dries (harmless)Recrisp restores; never stack/cover
Potatoes (final)Wire rack, room temp, single layer~10 minCrust softensUncovered, never cover
CarrotsCovered pan, residual heat15 minGlaze tightensLoosen with splash of water off-heat
Green beansDrained, dry, room temp15 minLose glossButter + zest toss at 6:57
JusWarm, lowest gas30 minOver-reducesLoosen with stock; re-strain
HorseradishFridge, coveredDaysNoneServe cold
## Plating Window Beef out of blast ~7:00–7:02 when crust set; 2–3 min handling/transfer (not a formal rest). 7:05 carve against the grain, ~1 cm. Plate carrots at 6:57, beans tossed in butter + zest at 6:57; jus + horseradish to table. ## Meal Balance Audit Richness: beef + duck fat + butter jus — high, relieved by green beans (fresh-firm reset), horseradish (cold sharp cut), and lemon zest aroma. Acid: horseradish (cultured cream + vinegar) and wine reduction across the savoury plate; lemon juice as adjustment. Distinct roles throughout — no redundancy. Sweet: carrots (light honey), single and isolated. Texture: crisp potato + beef crust vs. tender beef + soft carrots, green beans as firm anchor. No monotony, no accumulation gap. $m$, shared_prep_md=coalesce(nullif(shared_prep_md,''),$m$- **Lemon:** zest 1 → beans; juice → reserve for adjustments (horseradish, carrots, jus). - **Butter (cold, cubed):** 60 g total — 20 g → jus mount, 20 g → carrots, 20 g → beans. - **Diamond Crystal salt:** 12 g → beef brine (Sat); remainder to season potatoes/carrots/beans to taste. - **Jus base:** 1 sliced shallot browned in a little oil (default); beef trimmings optional additive. *Sourcing: Ask the butcher for trimmings when collecting the roast — free jus-base boost. Horseradish cream: taste before adding lemon or salt — prepared horseradish carries its own vinegar and salt.*$m$) where slug=$m$rib-eye-roast-sunday$m$;

update public.dish set method_md=$m$## Dish Overview MB3+ boneless rib eye roasted low to an even medium-rare, then blasted hot for a single deep crust. Uniform rosy interior wall-to-wall, deep-browned exterior, beef unmasked. Crust built once, at the end. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: serves 3 with leftovers · Total ~3.5 hr incl. temper · Active ~25 min · Oven 250°F → max* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseRendered beef fat + oil film for sear conduction
Primary driverThe beef — MB3+ marbling; no competing element
AcidNone in the roast — externalized to horseradish + jus (meal-level)
Aromatic/finishBlack pepper; thyme background
*Meal-level carve-out: acid provided by horseradish and jus, not the roast.* ## Texture Two distinct — yielding interior vs. crisp-browned crust. The final blast is the entire crust mechanism. ## Prep Phase 1. Sat: cut + re-tie done, 1.18 kg. Salt all surfaces evenly (12 g). Rack, uncovered, fridge, ~24 hr — dries surface, seasons deep. 1% is moderate and sufficient; the meat needs no finishing salt by default — taste a slice first. 2. 3:45pm Sun: out of fridge, ~70 min before roasting — takes the surface chill off; do not wait for the center to reach room temp. Pat bone-dry before roasting. 3. 4:50pm: rub with 1 tbsp oil, crack pepper all over. No additional salt. ## Active Cooking 1. Oven 250°F / 121°C. Leave-in probe (ThermoWorks) into thickest center, alarm 116°F. 2. Roast to pull — probe-governed (~75–80 min; 12 cm diameter drives this, not weight). Pull at 119–120°F / 48–49°C. 3. Rest uncovered on rack ~39 min (40 min ceiling). Oven → 450°F for potato recrisp, then → max in the final minutes. 4. Final blast: into max oven (500°F / 260°C), 5–8 min, crust-color-governed. A 1.18 kg roast climbs fast — watch it. 5. Verify: Thermapen the center post-blast. Expect ~127–133°F / 53–56°C — verify, don't assume a fixed rise. The probe number is the truth. ## Holding & Assembly Off the blast, 2–3 min handling/transfer (not a formal rest — the pre-blast rest already redistributed juices). Carve against the grain, ~1 cm. Jus + horseradish to table. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalOvershoot core — pulled too high or blasted too long. Cue: Thermapen >133°F post-blast → past medium-rare, grey bandUnrecoverable. Prevention: pull 119–120°F, blast by crust color not clock, verify with Thermapen
MajorWeak crust — surface not dry, or oven didn't recover to max. Cue: pale exterior after blastExtend blast 1–2 min watching center; if core near limit, accept lighter crust (serviceable)
MinorOff-center probe → uneven read. Cue: one end more doneCosmetic — serve to preference
## Adjustment Notes The meat is moderately salted from the brine — taste a slice before any finishing salt; jus and horseradish also carry salt. If flat, a few flakes at the plate, not the board. ## Scaling Notes Diameter governs low-roast time more than weight — 12 cm compact runs ~75–80 min. A long/narrow roast of the same weight runs faster with more crust. Below 1 kg, drop blast to 4–5 min. $m$, summary=coalesce(nullif(summary,''),$m$MB3+ boneless rib eye dry-brined 24 hr, roasted at 250°F to a probe-governed 119–120°F pull, rested under 40 min, then blasted in a max oven for a single deep crust and an even medium-rare (~127–133°F).$m$), servings=coalesce(servings,3), equipment=case when coalesce(array_length(equipment,1),0)=0 then array[$m$Bosch oven$m$,$m$wire rack$m$,$m$leave-in probe thermometer (ThermoWorks)$m$,$m$Thermapen$m$]::text[] else equipment end, designed_unvalidated=case when coalesce(jsonb_array_length(designed_unvalidated),0)=0 then $m$[{"param": "Post-blast core temperature", "designed_value": "~127–133°F / 53–56°C from a 119–120°F pull", "note": "Doc: 'verify, don't assume a fixed rise. The probe number is the truth.'"}, {"param": "Low-roast duration", "designed_value": "~75–80 min at 250°F for 12 cm diameter", "note": "Probe-governed; diameter drives it, not weight"}, {"param": "Final blast duration", "designed_value": "5–8 min at max / 500°F", "note": "Crust-color-governed; 1.18 kg climbs fast"}]$m$::jsonb else designed_unvalidated end, source=coalesce(nullif(source,''),$m$Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)$m$), governance_version=coalesce(governance_version,null), protein=coalesce(protein,$m$Beef$m$), category=case when coalesce(array_length(category,1),0)=0 then array[$m$Main$m$]::text[] else category end, difficulty=coalesce(difficulty,$m$Medium$m$) where slug=$m$ribeye-reverse-seared-rib-eye-roast$m$;

update public.dish set method_md=$m$## Dish Overview Parboiled potatoes pre-roasted to set, held, then recrisped during the beef rest — a shattering craggy crust and fluffy interior in duck fat. Baking soda in the parboil raises surface pH so the exterior crisps aggressively. The split solves the single-oven bottleneck. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: serves 3 · Total ~55 min across two phases · Active ~15 min · Oven 450°F / 230°C* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseDuck fat (roasting medium + flavor)
Primary driverPotato + duck fat richness
AcidNone — externalized to meal
Aromatic/finishGarlic + thyme in the fat; salt at finish
*Single-stage acceptable: no acid by design; richness component, acid externalized.* ## Texture Two distinct — craggy crisp shell vs. fluffy interior, via baking-soda parboil + roughing-up. ## Prep Phase 1. Peel (skin blocks crust and steams under the fat). Even ~4 cm chunks. 2. Parboil in salted water + ¼ tsp baking soda, ~8 min from boil, until edges just soften. 3. Drain thoroughly, dry in the hot pan 30 sec, then shake hard in the colander to rough the surfaces — roughed edges become the crust. ## Active Cooking 1. Pre-roast: heat duck fat in the tray in the 450°F oven ~5 min until shimmering. Add potatoes (dry — spatter risk), turn to coat, add garlic/thyme if using. Roast to pale gold and structurally set, ~25–30 min. Remove; hold uncovered, single layer, wire rack, room temp. 2. Recrisp: once the oven has recovered to ≥425–450°F during the beef rest, return potatoes ~15–20 min, turning once, until deeply golden and audibly crisp. Salt out of the oven. ## Holding & Assembly Pre-roasted potatoes hold up to ~2 hr on the rack, room temp. Final crisped potatoes hold ~10 min. Never stack or cover at any stage — trapped steam softens the crust instantly. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorSoft, greasy — fat not hot at entry, or crowded tray. Cue: pale, oil-slickedSpread out, raise to 475°F, extend. Prevention: fat shimmering before entry; single layer
MajorOver-browned crags / scorched garlic on recrisp — too long at true 450°F. Cue: dark bitter edges, acrid garlicRecoverable for potatoes (pull immediately); discard scorched aromatics. Prevention: sensory-govern the recrisp, pull when golden not dark
MinorOver-roughed → mushy exterior. Cue: edges disintegrate on turningCosmetic — still crisps
## Adjustment Notes Salt only out of the oven — earlier salt draws moisture, softens crust. Undercrisp at service → a few more minutes, but this competes with the beef blast; accept as-is if the beef needs the oven. ## Scaling Notes Do not crowd — potatoes need space. Above 700 g, use two trays or the crust fails across the batch. $m$, summary=coalesce(nullif(summary,''),$m$Peeled Yukon/Maris potatoes parboiled with baking soda, roughed up, pre-roasted in shimmering duck fat at 450°F to set, held on a rack, then recrisped ~15–20 min during the beef rest for a craggy shattering crust.$m$), servings=coalesce(servings,3), equipment=case when coalesce(array_length(equipment,1),0)=0 then array[$m$Bosch oven$m$,$m$roasting tray$m$,$m$colander$m$,$m$wire rack$m$]::text[] else equipment end, designed_unvalidated=case when coalesce(jsonb_array_length(designed_unvalidated),0)=0 then $m$[{"param": "Pre-roast duration", "designed_value": "~25–30 min at 450°F to pale gold, structurally set", "note": "Sensory-governed"}, {"param": "Recrisp duration", "designed_value": "~15–20 min at ≥425–450°F, turning once", "note": "Pull when deeply golden and audibly crisp; competes with beef blast for the oven"}, {"param": "Pre-roast hold", "designed_value": "up to ~2 hr on wire rack, room temp", "note": "Surface dries (harmless); recrisp restores"}]$m$::jsonb else designed_unvalidated end, source=coalesce(nullif(source,''),$m$Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)$m$), governance_version=coalesce(governance_version,null), protein=coalesce(protein,null), category=case when coalesce(array_length(category,1),0)=0 then array[$m$Side$m$]::text[] else category end, difficulty=coalesce(difficulty,$m$Medium$m$) where slug=$m$ribeye-roast-potatoes$m$;

*Acid single-stage at finish justified: glaze reduction; acid's role is corrective, not structural.* ## Texture Meal-level texture exemption — glazed carrots are inherently soft; contrast provided by crisp potatoes and beef crust across the plate. ## Prep Phase 1. Peel (skin turns leathery and bitter under a glaze). Even ~5 cm batons. ## Active Cooking 1. Carrots, butter, 1 tsp honey, ~50 ml water, pinch salt in a pan on induction 1. Cover, medium, ~8 min until a knife meets slight resistance. 2. Uncover, raise heat, reduce to a glossy glaze, ~4–5 min. Toss to coat. 3. MinorUndercooked core. Cue: knife meets hard resistanceSplash water, cover, 2–3 min more
## Adjustment Notes Too sweet → lemon squeeze. Flat → pinch of salt sharpens. Don't add honey at the end — won't integrate off-heat. ## Scaling Notes Not applicable. $m$,3,array[$m$induction hob$m$,$m$lidded pan$m$]::text[],$m$[{"param": "Covered cook time", "designed_value": "~8 min, medium, until knife meets slight resistance", "note": "Then ~4–5 min uncovered reduction to glaze"}]$m$::jsonb,null);

MinorZest added on heat → bitter. Cue: acrid edgePrevention: zest off-heat only, at the very end
## Adjustment Notes Zest is the default for brightness without added sharpness; a few drops of lemon juice off-heat are a valid post-cook correction if it needs lift. BaseCrème fraîche
Primary driverHorseradish heat + pungency
AcidCrème fraîche tang + vinegar inherent to prepared horseradish; optional lemon
Aromatic/finish—

Its job is flavor (sharp/cold), not texture. ## Prep Phase 1. Fold horseradish into crème fraîche. Taste before adding anything — prepared horseradish already carries vinegar and salt. Then adjust: pinch of salt if flat, lemon if it needs lift, more horseradish for bite. ## Active Cooking None. ## Holding & Assembly Fridge, covered, up to several days. update public.dish set method_md=$m$## Dish Overview A concentrated red-wine-and-stock reduction built on browned shallot — not dependent on roast-pan fond, which a 250°F roast won't reliably produce. Staged with a hold to preserve the make-ahead without over-concentrating. Low-roast and post-blast drippings fold in as available. Reduced to a light nappe, mounted with cold butter. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: ~150 ml · Total ~45 min across stages · Active ~15 min · Outdoor gas* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseBrowned shallot fond (+ optional trimmings), built independently in the saucepan
Primary driverReduced beef stock + wine depth
AcidRed wine — staged early, reduced; acidity mellows and integrates
Aromatic/finishCold butter mount for gloss + body
*Acid staged correctly: wine in early, reduced to depth not sharpness.* ## Texture Meal-level exemption — a sauce; target is a light-syrup nappe coating a spoon back. ## Prep Phase 1. Finely slice 1 shallot. If using trimmings, have them ready. ## Active Cooking (staged) 1. Stage 1 (~4:45pm): brown shallot (+ optional trimmings) in a little oil over medium until deeply colored. Deglaze with wine, scraping the pan; reduce by half, ~5 min. Add stock, bring to a brief simmer, then off heat, covered. 2. Stage 2 (~6:05pm): return to gas, finish reducing to ~150 ml, lightly syrupy. Fold in low-roast drippings once the beef pulls. 3. Stage 3 (~6:40–6:43pm): off-heat, whisk in cold butter for gloss. Strain. Taste — salt sparingly (stock + drippings already salty). Hold warm on lowest gas. 4. After the beef's blast, pour any last drippings into the finished sauce and re-warm briefly. ## Holding & Assembly Warm on lowest gas up to 30 min. If sticky, loosen with a splash of stock and re-strain. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorOver-reduced sticky/salty — reduced too far, or not held between stages. Cue: coats too thick, concentrated-saltyLoosen with stock/water; don't add salt. Prevention: stage with the off-heat hold; taste before final reduction
MinorButter mount breaks — added on too-high heat. Cue: oily, splitOff-heat, whisk in a splash of cold stock to re-emulsify
## Adjustment Notes If flat, a few drops of reserved lemon juice or a splash of wine lifts it. Salt last and sparingly — reduction concentrates existing salt. ## Scaling Notes Not applicable. $m$, summary=coalesce(nullif(summary,''),$m$Shallot-based red wine and beef stock reduction built independently of pan fond in three staged steps with an off-heat hold, enriched with roast drippings as available, reduced to ~150 ml light nappe and mounted with cold butter.$m$), servings=coalesce(servings,3), equipment=case when coalesce(array_length(equipment,1),0)=0 then array[$m$outdoor gas burner$m$,$m$saucepan$m$,$m$fine strainer$m$,$m$whisk$m$]::text[] else equipment end, designed_unvalidated=case when coalesce(jsonb_array_length(designed_unvalidated),0)=0 then $m$[{"param": "Wine reduction", "designed_value": "reduce by half, ~5 min", "note": "Stage 1"}, {"param": "Final volume", "designed_value": "~150 ml, lightly syrupy (light nappe)", "note": "Stage 2; taste before final reduction"}, {"param": "Warm hold", "designed_value": "up to 30 min on lowest gas", "note": "Loosen with stock and re-strain if sticky"}]$m$::jsonb else designed_unvalidated end, source=coalesce(nullif(source,''),$m$Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)$m$), governance_version=coalesce(governance_version,null), protein=coalesce(protein,null), category=case when coalesce(array_length(category,1),0)=0 then array[$m$Sauce$m$]::text[] else category end, difficulty=coalesce(difficulty,$m$Medium$m$) where slug=$m$ribeye-jus$m$;
